newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's imports up 11.2 pct in May vs yr ago.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's imports up 11.2 pct in May vs yr ago.

text.p: The value of Venezuela's imports continued their steady rise, jumping $101 million, or 11.2 percent, in May to $999 million from $898 million in May 1996, according to the Central Office of Statistics and Information (OCEI).
Imports for the first five months of the year were up $720 million, or 20.6 percent, at $4.211 billion, compared with $3.491 billion in the same period of 1996, the OCEI said in a release.
Imports in May were up $13 million, or 1.5 percent, from $885 million in April.
The private sector accounted for the vast majority of imports in the first five months of 1997, with 86 percent of the total.
"Electrical materials" was the biggest category of imports with 31.0 percent of the total. "Chemical Products" followed with 10.8 percent, then "Common Metals" with 10.6 percent.

The United States was the top exporter to Venezuela with 48.3 percent, followed by Brazil and Germany with 4.9 percent each, Colombia with 4.8 percent, Japan with 3.6 percent and Italy with 3.0 percent.
